The proposed answer is incorrect. The correct value is $1+2i$.

Multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1-2i$:

$$\frac{-3+4i}{1+2i}=\frac{(-3+4i)(1-2i)}{(1+2i)(1-2i)}=\frac{-3+6i+4i-8i^2}{5}=\frac{5+10i}{5}=1+2i$$

Check: $(1+2i)(1+2i)=1+4i+4i^2=-3+4i$.

The shortcut fails because changing the numerator's sign does not simply flip the sign of the imaginary part of the quotient. The denominator $1+2i$ is unchanged, so the result is not the conjugate of the original quotient.
